8
A tennis ball of mass 55 g is travelling horizontally with a speed of 30 m s–1. The ball makes
contact with a wall before rebounding in the horizontal direction with a speed of 20 m s–1. The ball
is in contact with the wall for a time of 5.0 × 10–3
s.
What is the average force exerted on the wall by the ball?
A
110 N
B
220 N
C
330 N
D
550 N

hints: Notice the ball reverses direction from $30 \text{ m s}^{-1}$ toward the wall to $20 \text{ m s}^{-1}$ away, so the change in velocity is larger than either speed alone.
Recall that average force is linked to rate of change of momentum by $F = \Delta p / \Delta t$, with $\Delta p = m\Delta v$ and mass $55 \text{ g} = 0.055 \text{ kg}$.
Calculate the magnitude of $\Delta v$ allowing for the sign change, then divide $m\Delta v$ by the contact time $5.0 \times 10^{-3} \text{ s}$ and use Newton's third law for the force on the wall.
walkthrough: Take the direction toward the wall as positive. Then initial velocity is $+30 \text{ m s}^{-1}$ and final velocity after rebound is $-20 \text{ m s}^{-1}$.
Average force on the ball follows from impulse: $F\Delta t = \Delta p = m(v - u)$. Convert mass to kilograms: $m = 55 \text{ g} = 0.055 \text{ kg}$.
Find the velocity change: $v - u = -20 - (+30) = -50 \text{ m s}^{-1}$, so the magnitude of change is $50 \text{ m s}^{-1}$.
Find the magnitude of momentum change: $\lvert \Delta p \rvert = 0.055 \times 50 = 2.75 \text{ kg m s}^{-1}$.
Divide by contact time to get average force magnitude: $F = 2.75 / (5.0 \times 10^{-3}) = 550 \text{ N}$.
By Newton's third law the wall exerts $550 \text{ N}$ on the ball, so the ball exerts $550 \text{ N}$ on the wall. This is option D.

A.explanation: This uses a speed change of only $10 \text{m s}^{-1}$ from $30-20$, ignoring that rebound reverses direction so the changes add.

B.explanation: This uses only the rebound speed of $20 \text{m s}^{-1}$, giving $0.055 \times 20 / 5.0 \times 10^{-3} = 220 \text{ N}$ instead of the total change in momentum.

C.explanation: This uses only the incident speed of $30 \text{m s}^{-1}$, giving $0.055 \times 30 / 5.0 \times 10^{-3} = 330 \text{ N}$ instead of the total change in momentum.

D.explanation: The total velocity change on reversal is $50 \text{m s}^{-1}$, giving $0.055 \times 50 / 5.0 \times 10^{-3} = 550 \text{ N}$ on the wall.
